newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals face resistance levels.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals face resistance levels.

text.p: The precious metals markets faced a critical day on Wednesday as gold, silver and platinum prices all faced up to key resistance areas, dealers said.
Gold, which has been lagging silver and platinum so far, was key to the continuing uptrend.
"The white metals (silver and platinum) led the way up but now gold needs to start participating," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $382.50 per ounce against $381.90 previously and a close of $381.50/$382.00.
Support came in from New York late Tuesday and in the Far East, where the price was sustained on two-way business.
Dealers in Hong Kong noted that what was believed to be Australian producer business coming in at $382.40 was being countered by buying on European accounts up to $383.00.
"There's been a lot of two-way business. There's a bit of a battle going on at these levels," one dealer said.
Fairly brisk buying in early European dealing might have been mainly professionals taking positions as gold and silver approached critical levels, he added.
The historical price charts looked positive overall now that gold had broken out of its narrow $387-$381 price band.
But gold faced a major challenge to reach its target for Wednesday at $383.50. "That looks feasible," a dealer said, adding that resistance above that figure would be testing.

"The $383.50-$384.50 is the resistance area. If it can get through $384.50-$385.00, the level from which it broke before, then it could get to $388.00-$390.00," a dealer said, adding that this was "a long way".
He added, "If there are any longer term shorts around, then $385.00 is likely to be where the buy stops would be for them to come in and cover."
Silver was at $4.89/$4.91, up three cents. Its resistance began at $4.92, clearance of which could lead to $4.98.
Dealers said there had been professional buying of silver earlier, suggesting positions taken for a test of the resistance.
Platinum was steady but a little easier at $387.25/$388.25, having been bought on the basis of Tuesday's report by refiner Johnson Matthey forecasting a tighter market this year.
"The widening platinum-gold spread also helped platinum as players started off short of platinum and long of gold, then had to buy platinum as the spread widened," a dealer said.
"That helped platinum and may have helped to cap gold," he added.
